2299250.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA TO ADDRESS THE NATION TOMORROW ON THE EVE OF 80TH INDEPENDENCE DAY
2299250.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA TO ADDRESS THE NATION TOMORROW ON THE EVE OF 80TH INDEPENDENCE DAY
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 10:14PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu will address the nation tomorrow (August 14, 2026) on the eve of the 80th Independence Day.

The address will be broadcast from 1900 hrs. on the entire national network of Akashvani and telecast over all channels of Doordarshan in Hindi followed by the English version. Broadcast of the address in Hindi and English on Doordarshan will be followed by broadcast in regional languages by regional channels of Doordarshan. Akashvani will broadcast regional language versions at 2130 hrs. on its respective regional networks.

 

***

2299217.title: Union Minister for Law & Justice (I/C) Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal launches revamped India Code Portal at the Legislative Department
2299217.body_html:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Union Minister for Law & Justice (I/C) Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal launches revamped India Code Portal at the Legislative Department
Revamped portal to make access to laws simpler, faster and more citizen-centric
AI-assisted search, semantic and speech search, improved navigation and multilingual access among key features
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 8:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, today, on 13th August, 2026, launched the revamped India Code Portal at Kartavya Bhavan 2, New Delhi, in the august presence of Shri R. Venkataramani, Attorney General for India, Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs, Dr. Manoj Kumar, Additional Secretary, and senior officers of the Legislative Department. Shri Priyank Bharti, Director General, National Informatics Centre (NIC), Shri Sudeep Shrivastava, Chief Operating Officer, IndiaAI Mission and senior officers of the NIC were also present on the occasion.

The revamped portal marks an important step in the Government’s continuing endeavour to make access to laws simpler, faster, wider and more citizen-centric, using contemporary digital technologies.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal underscored the importance of the Constitution and of ensuring that laws are easily accessible, understandable and available to all stakeholders. He observed that the India Code Portal serves as a reliable and comprehensive platform for citizen-friendly access to the Constitution, Central Acts, Rules and other legislative information. Highlighting the role of technology in strengthening access to law, he appreciated the dedicated efforts of the officers and officials of the Legislative Department in conceptualising, coordinating and overseeing the revamp, as well as the NIC team for its technical expertise and development support. Shri Meghwal noted that this collaborative effort would significantly enhance the accessibility, transparency and citizen-centric delivery of legislative information.

Shri R. Venkataramani, Attorney General for India, highlighted the transformation from physical to digital access to laws and appreciated the revamped India Code Portal developed by the Legislative Department with several new and user-friendly features. He emphasized the importance of keeping the portal technologically updated and responsive to emerging requirements. He also stressed the responsibility of legislative officers to contribute towards clear, effective and quality legislation and underscored the importance of ensuring wider and convenient access to laws. He appreciated the coordinated efforts of the Legislative Department and the technical team in developing the revamped portal, which would further strengthen transparency and public access to legislative information.

Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs, outlined the evolution of the India Code Portal and the efforts to make authentic and updated legislative information easily accessible to citizens, legal professionals, government departments and other stakeholders. Highlighting the role of technology in improving dissemination and access to laws, he outlined the key features of the revamped portal, including its more user-friendly interface and enhanced search, navigation and accessibility. He appreciated the coordinated efforts of the Legislative Department and the National Informatics Centre (NIC) and expressed confidence that the revamped platform would significantly strengthen wider and easier public access to reliable legislative information.

Dr Manoj Kumar, Additional Secretary, Legislative Department, introduced the revamped India Code Portal and outlined its key features and the larger vision behind its transformation. He observed that access to law is the first step towards access to justice and that laws must not only be available, but also easy to find, navigate, understand and use. He highlighted that the revamped portal seeks to move India Code beyond being a repository of legislative documents towards becoming an accessible, interconnected and citizen-centric digital gateway to law, with improved search and navigation, linkages between Acts and subordinate legislation, integration with the e-Gazette ecosystem, AI-assisted and semantic search, speech-enabled access and multilingual capabilities. He emphasised that technology should reduce the distance between the law and the citizen and enable legislative information to become more discoverable, interoperable and usable, thereby strengthening transparency, legal awareness and citizen-centric governance.

India Code provides a unified digital repository of Central Acts and their subordinate legislations, State Acts and their subordinate legislations, as well as Union Territory legislations and regulations. The revamped portal significantly enhances the manner in which citizens, legal professionals, researchers, the judiciary and Government can search, navigate and access legislative information through improved and intelligent search capabilities, AI-assisted search and interaction, semantic and speech-based search, easier navigation across legislations, access to amendments and legislative history, linkage of Acts with relevant subordinate legislation, integration with the e-Gazette ecosystem, improved document viewing, QR-enabled access and a structured citizen-feedback mechanism. It also seeks to enable AI-assisted multilingual access to laws in all 22 languages included in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution, thereby making access to law wider, easier and more citizen-centric across Bharat.

The technological revamp seeks to transform India Code from being merely an online repository of legislation into a digital gateway to law, supported by an increasingly interconnected and citizen-friendly legal information architecture.

The initiative is aligned with the larger objective of leveraging technology for ease of accessing law, transparency, wider citizen participation and improved delivery of legal and public services.

The revamped India Code Portal represents an important step towards building a trusted and technology-enabled legal information ecosystem for Bharat, where laws are increasingly searchable, accessible, interconnected and available to citizens in the language and form most convenient to them.

2299208.title: DRI busts illegal drug manufacturing facility in Jewar, UP; 30 kg drugs seized and two persons arrested
2299208.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI busts illegal drug manufacturing facility in Jewar, UP; 30 kg drugs seized and two persons arrested
30 kg precursor chemicals to be used for manufacture of drugs, and complete equipment and apparatus also seized
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has busted another clandestine drug manufacturing facility. The facility was found operating from a residential premises in the Jewar area of Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh.

On 09/10 Aug 2026, an intelligence-led operation of DRI, resulted in the seizure of approximately 30 kg Amphetamine/intermediary forms, around 30 kg precursor chemicals, to be used for manufacture of drugs, and complete equipment and apparatus used for clandestine manufacture of psychotropic substances.

Various chemicals, equipment and contraband recovered from the premise.

 

Search of the premises revealed a fully equipped clandestine manufacturing set-up, comprising electrical furnaces, hose pipes, scientific and measuring equipment, reagents and other equipment and tools required for manufacture of psychotropic substances. Multiple liquid containers containing various precursor chemicals, raw materials and reagents were also recovered from the premises, along with white-coloured powdery/crystalline substances stored in different containers, whose testing with field kits indicated the presence of amphetamine, a psychotropic substance scheduled under Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act 1985.

The recoveries, along with the manufacturing apparatus, amphetamine and chemicals found at the premises, indicate the existence of a clandestine facility being used for illicit manufacture of psychotropic substances in contravention of the provisions of the (NDPS) Act, 1985.  A foreign national and his Indian female associate, who were operating the clandestine facility, were arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985.

Preliminary investigation indicated the accused persons would bring manufacturing equipment and raw materials to the premises during night hours, set up and operate the facility for about a week, and thereafter would remove the equipment and clean the premises. The same cycle was reportedly repeated after a gap of two to three months, apparently to avoid suspicion among local residents.

Recent DRI action against clandestine drug manufacturing

The present operation is result of DRI's intensified focus on dismantling clandestine drug manufacturing infrastructure and the networks supporting illicit production and trafficking. In the past one month, DRI has busted three other clandestine manufacturing facilities—a Mephedrone manufacturing facility at Ankleshwar, Gujarat, where Mephedrone and substantial quantities of precursor chemicals were seized and three persons arrested; an Alprazolam and Diazepam manufacturing facility in Satara, Maharashtra, where finished and intermediary psychotropic substances and approximately 400 litres of raw materials were seized and two persons arrested; and a Tramadol manufacturing and export network centred in Ambernath, Maharashtra, linked to an attempted export of 1 lakh Tramadol to Nigeria, resulting in the arrest of three key accused persons.

These successive operations demonstrate DRI's continued focus on identifying and dismantling the entire ecosystem of illicit drug manufacture—from procurement of precursor chemicals and establishment of clandestine laboratories to financing, trafficking, storage and attempted export of narcotics drugs and psychotropic substances. The operations also highlight the increasingly sophisticated methods adopted by drug trafficking networks to conceal manufacturing activities and evade detection.

2299186.title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Milestone achieved in global climate action
2299186.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2299186.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Milestone achieved in global climate action
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 8:11PM by PIB Delhi

India’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) comprises of three quantitative targets namely the reduction of overall emissions intensity of our Gross Domestic Product (GDP), enhancing share of non-fossil fuel-based energy resources in installed electric power capacity and creation of additional carbon sink.

India had achieved a reduction of 37.38% in the emissions intensity of its GDP in 2022 from the  2005 level, against the NDC goal of reducing emissions intensity by 45% by 2030. The share of  cumulative installed electric power capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy sources crossed 50%  in June 2025, thereby achieving the NDC goal five years ahead of the committed timeline. As of  30th June 2026, non-fossil fuel-based energy resources accounted for 54.18% of the country’s total installed electric power capacity. India has created an additional carbon sink of 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent during 2005 to 2022, against the NDC goal of creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5–3.0 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2030 through additional forest and tree cover.

As reported in India’s first Biennial Transparency Report submitted to the United Nations  Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in April, 2026, the decoupling of  greenhouse gas emissions from economic growth and GDP can be attributed to policies promoting  renewable energy deployment, improving the energy efficiency of all economic activity. The early achievement of NDC goal on share of non-fossil fuel based installed electric power capacity has been made possible by a range of policies that incentivize renewable energy generation and its integration in to national electricity grid. The creation of carbon sink could be possible because of high priority accorded to conservation and restoration by the national and the State governments. The approach is reflected in the framework of Policies, Acts, Rules, Programmes and Schemes to ensure conservation of forests and biodiversity, enhance green cover and participation of people in the conservation activities while protecting rights of forest dependent communities.

The NDC targets for the year 2035 have been enhanced, with quantitative targets to reduce the emissions intensity of GDP by 47% from the 2005 level, achieve 60% cumulative installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy resources, and create carbon sink of 3.5 to 4.0 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent through forest and tree cover as compared to the baseline year of

2005. The NDC also includes five qualitative targets aimed at promoting sustainable lifestyles, enhancing adaptation capacity and adoption of climate friendly cleaner path aligned with the goal of Viksit Bharat @2047.

India's progress in implementing its significant climate commitments has received wide recognition from many leading international bodies including the International Energy Agency (IEA), Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), United Nationals Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), World Bank, International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), etc.

This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.

2299181.title: Government Strengthens Welfare, Healthcare and Social Security Measures for Senior Citizens
2299181.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Government Strengthens Welfare, Healthcare and Social Security Measures for Senior Citizens
AVYAY, Healthcare and Social Security Measures Strengthen Support for India’s Growing Elderly Population
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 8:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has taken a comprehensive range of measures to address the growing needs of senior citizens and ensure their welfare, healthcare, social security and dignified living.

According to written information provided by the Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B.L. Verma in the Lok Sabha to Shri Yadhuveer Wadiyar, India’s elderly population is projected to increase from 10 crore in 2011 to 23 crore by 2036, with its share in the total population rising from 8.4 per cent to 14.9 per cent.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) as an umbrella scheme for the welfare of senior citizens across the country. The scheme comprises seven components covering areas such as shelter and care, State-level interventions, grievance redressal, assistive devices, innovative solutions, geriatric caregiving and other initiatives for healthy and productive ageing.

During the last three years, from 2023-24 to 2025-26, a total of 10,00,456 beneficiaries were covered under AVYAY, 2,21,30,687 beneficiaries under NSAP and 28,29,63,879 beneficiaries under NPHCE.

Under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC), grants-in-aid are provided to Non-Governmental and Voluntary Organisations for running and maintaining Senior Citizens Homes and Continuous Care Homes, where indigent senior citizens are provided facilities including shelter, nutrition, Medicare and entertainment free of cost. The State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC) supports States and Union Territories for activities including awareness generation, sensitisation, cataract surgeries and other State-specific initiatives.

The Government has also strengthened grievance redressal and support services through Elderline, the National Helpline for Senior Citizens. The toll-free helpline 14567, launched on October 1, 2021, provides grievance redressal services and generates awareness among senior citizens regarding relevant Acts, schemes and programmes of the Central and State Governments.

Under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY), senior citizens with a monthly income of not more than ₹15,000 and suffering from age-related disabilities or infirmities are provided physical aids and assisted-living devices aimed at restoring near-normal bodily functions. The scheme, launched on April 1, 2017, is implemented through Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO), a Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

The Seniorcare Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE) component promotes innovative solutions for problems commonly faced by the elderly. Innovative start-ups are identified and encouraged to develop products, processes and services for the welfare of senior citizens, with Government investment in the equity of selected firms not exceeding 49 per cent of their total equity.

To address the increasing demand for professional elderly care, the Government is also implementing the Training of Geriatric Care Givers component, aimed at bridging the gap between the supply and demand for trained geriatric caregivers and creating a professional cadre in the field of geriatric care.

Healthcare support for senior citizens is being strengthened through initiatives of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Under Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), health insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh is provided to all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their socio-economic status.

The National Programme for Healthcare of the Elderly (NPHCE) focuses on the health and well-being of senior citizens through a community-based primary healthcare approach, dedicated services at Primary and Community Health Centre levels, dedicated facilities at district hospitals, strengthening of Regional Geriatric Centres and information and education initiatives. The programme also provides for continuous monitoring, independent evaluation and research in geriatrics. The tertiary component of the Rashtriya Varishth Jan Swasthya Yojana has resulted in the establishment of 17 Regional Geriatric Centres and two National Centres of Ageing.

Social security support is also provided through the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development. Under the programme, eligible senior citizens receive a central pension share of ₹200 per month for those aged 60–79 years and ₹500 per month for those aged 80 years and above, with States and Union Territories providing additional top-ups.

The Government conducts periodic assessments of AVYAY to review its implementation and outcomes. Discussions are held with stakeholders to assess emerging needs and challenges faced by senior citizens, while third-party evaluations are undertaken before continuation of the scheme during a new financial cycle. The findings and recommendations of these evaluations are used to review implementation and identify emerging needs, with appropriate steps taken to mitigate hardships faced by senior citizens.

The Government’s multi-dimensional approach combines social care, healthcare, pension support, grievance redressal, assistive devices, geriatric caregiving and innovation to respond to the evolving needs of the country’s senior citizen population and promote a life of dignity, security and well-being for the elderly.

2299179.title: Transforming Education through Smart Classrooms in SC-Dominated Villages: A Digital Learning Initiative in Kathua, Jammu and Kashmir
2299179.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Transforming Education through Smart Classrooms in SC-Dominated Villages: A Digital Learning Initiative in Kathua, Jammu and Kashmir
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 8:02PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY), District Kathua has taken significant strides towards bridging the digital divide in rural and border areas by establishing Smart Classrooms in Government Schools located in SC-dominated villages.

During the year 2022-23, a total of 07 Smart Classrooms were established under the PM-AJAY component in different Government Schools of SC-dominated villages. Notably, these included Chack Chabba and Chack Nathal, villages located near the International Border, and Village Sandhi, situated in the remotest sub-division of Bani. Each Smart Classroom included installation of Interactive Touch Panels, procurement of student furniture, and execution of essential civil works such as child-friendly wall paintings and electrification.

Building upon this success, 04 additional Smart Classrooms were established during 2023-24 under the same component. Further, in 2025-26, 03 more Smart Classrooms were added, thereby expanding the outreach of digital education in the district.

The establishment of Smart Classrooms has significantly enhanced the overall learning experience of students in rural and far-flung areas. Access to modern teaching tools, audio-visual content, and interactive learning—once limited to expensive private schools—has now reached Government Schools in remote villages with limited exposure to the outside world. For many students, modern digital education, once a distant dream, has become a reality, leading to improved classroom engagement, conceptual clarity, and academic outcomes.

2299177.title: NMBA reaches, sensitizes more than 30.52 crore people across the country, this includes more than 11.87 crore youth and 8.45 crore women
2299177.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NMBA reaches, sensitizes more than 30.52 crore people across the country, this includes more than 11.87 crore youth and 8.45 crore women
Central Government Strengthens Drug Demand Reduction and Rehabilitation Services in Jammu & Kashmir
Over 1.20 Crore People Sensitized under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan in Jammu & Kashmir
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 8:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has undertaken a range of measures to strengthen prevention, treatment and rehabilitation services for substance use in Jammu & Kashmir under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), according to the reply given by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment in Rajya Sabha.

As per the National Survey on Extent and Pattern of Substance Use in India conducted by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment through the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS in 2018, opioids had a prevalence of 4.91 per cent in Jammu & Kashmir, with an estimated 5.40 lakh users in the 10–75 age group. Alcohol had a prevalence of 3.50 per cent with an estimated 3.90 lakh users, followed by sedatives at 1.54 per cent with 1.70 lakh estimated users, cannabis at 1.31 per cent with 1.40 lakh users and inhalants at 1.22 per cent with 1.35 lakh users.

In a written reply to Shri. Sajjad Ahmad Kichloo in the Rajya Sabha, the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B.L. Verma stated that the Government is supporting a network of treatment and rehabilitation facilities in Jammu & Kashmir. These include 1 Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA), 3 Outreach and Drop In Centres (ODICs), 2 Community based Peer Led Intervention (CPLI) programmes, 6 District De-Addiction Centres (DDACs) and 21 Addiction Treatment Facilities (ATFs).

The number of persons treated for drug addiction in centres supported by the Department in Jammu & Kashmir increased from 5,382 in 2021-22 to 46,491 in 2025-26. The annual figures were 27,843 in 2022-23, 36,588 in 2023-24 and 40,546 in 2024-25.

Under NAPDDR, the Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations for preventive education, awareness generation, capacity building and drug demand reduction programmes. Assistance is also provided to NGOs and voluntary organisations for running and maintaining IRCAs, CPLIs, ODICs and DDACs, while Government hospitals are supported for establishing Addiction Treatment Facilities.

Across the country, NAPDDR-supported activities include 344 IRCAs, 45 CPLI programmes, 76 ODICs, 155 ATFs and 145 DDACs. IRCAs provide in-patient treatment along with counselling, detoxification/de-addiction, after-care and reintegration into the social mainstream. CPLI programmes focus on children below 18 years, while ODICs provide screening, assessment, counselling and referral and linkage to treatment and rehabilitation services.

The Ministry also maintains the toll-free de-addiction helpline 14446, which provides primary counselling and immediate referral services to persons seeking help. More than 4.6 lakh calls have been received through the helpline so far, including more than 11,000 calls from Jammu & Kashmir.

The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), launched on August 15, 2020 in 272 identified vulnerable districts, has since August 2023 been extended to all districts of the country. The campaign focuses on spreading awareness about substance use, particularly among higher educational institutions, university campuses and schools. With the support of States, NMBA has so far reached and sensitized more than 30.52 crore people across the country, including more than 11.87 crore youth and 8.45 crore women. Over 28.61 Lakh activities have been conducted in educational institutions while more than 28.29 Lakh persons have been treated and rehabilitated across the country, as on this date.

In Jammu & Kashmir, the campaign has sensitized more than 1.20 crore people, including over 69.14 lakh youth and 51.20 lakh women, through extensive awareness and outreach activities. A total of 8,565 Nasha Mukt Mitrs have joined the campaign in the Union Territory.

2299174.title: Central Government Reaffirms Measures to Protect Rights and Promote Inclusion of LGBTQAI+ Community
2299174.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Central Government Reaffirms Measures to Protect Rights and Promote Inclusion of LGBTQAI+ Community
Measures cover legal protection, ration cards, banking, healthcare and safety of LGBTQAI+ community
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 7:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has reiterated its commitment to ensuring the protection of rights, welfare and social inclusion of the LGBTQAI+ community, including intersex persons, through a range of legal, administrative and welfare measures across different social spheres.

In a written reply to Smt Rajathi in the Rajya Sabha, the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B.L. Verma, outlined measures being undertaken by various Ministries and Departments to improve participation of the LGBTQAI+ community in areas including education, employment, identity documentation and other entitlements.

The Government's response highlighted a multi-Ministry approach towards strengthening protection, access to services and social inclusion of the LGBTQAI+ community, covering food security, financial services, healthcare, protection from discrimination, and safety and dignity.

The Ministry stated that the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, as amended in 2026, provides a comprehensive legal framework for the protection and welfare of transgender persons. The Act includes intersex persons born with congenital variations within the definition of transgender person. The Act and the Rules framed thereunder provide protection against discrimination and facilitate access to welfare measures and other entitlements.

The Department of Food and Public Distribution has issued an advisory to all States and Union Territories clarifying that, under existing provisions, partners in a queer relationship are to be treated as part of the same household for the purposes of ration cards. States and UTs have also been advised to take necessary measures to ensure that such partners do not face discrimination in the issuance of ration cards.

The Department of Financial Services has issued an advisory clarifying that there are no restrictions on persons of the queer community opening a joint bank account. The advisory also permits a person in a queer relationship to be nominated to receive the balance in the account in the event of the death of the account holder.

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has issued communications to stakeholders, including States and UTs, for ensuring the rights of the LGBTQAI+ community in relation to healthcare. The measures include awareness activities, prohibition of conversion therapy, availability of sex reassignment surgery, changes in curricula, tele-consultation facilities, sensitisation and training of staff at various levels, and provisions relating to claiming the body where no near relative, next of kin or family member is available.

The Directorate General of Health Services has also issued a communication to State Health Departments and other stakeholders regarding ensuring healthcare access and reducing discrimination towards the LGBTQAI+ community.

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has framed guidelines concerning medical intervention required for infants and children with disorders of sexual differentiation (intersex), with the objective of enabling them to lead a medically normal life without complications. The Ministry is also working on guidelines addressing issues relating to the mental health and well-being of the queer community.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has issued an advisory to all States and UTs concerning prison visitation rights of the queer community. Another advisory has been issued regarding law-and-order measures to ensure that members of the queer community do not face threats of violence, harassment or coercion.

2299122.title: INDIA AND KENYA SHARE HISTORICAL AND MULTIFACETED RELATIONS GOING BACK OVER MILLENNIA: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
2299122.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
INDIA AND KENYA SHARE HISTORICAL AND MULTIFACETED RELATIONS GOING BACK OVER MILLENNIA: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
KENYA SUPPORTS INDIA’S CANDIDATURE AS PERMANENT MEMBER OF UNITED NATIONS SECURITY COUNCIL (UNSC)
PARLIAMENTARY DELEGATION FROM KENYA CALLS ON LOK SABHA SPEAKER
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 7:12PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today said that India and Kenya share historical and multifaceted relations dating back millennia. He noted that regular high-level engagements have continuously strengthened the bilateral relationship between the two countries.

Shri Birla made these remarks during his bilateral meeting with Rt. Hon. (Dr.) Moses M. Wetang'ula, EGH, Speaker of the National Assembly of Kenya, at the Parliament House Complex today. Recalling his earlier meeting with Dr. Wetang'ula during the 28th CSPOC held in New Delhi earlier this year, he observed that Dr. Wetang'ula has extensive experience in public life and a distinguished career in law, legislation and administration, and has contributed significantly to strengthening governance for the benefit of the people of Kenya.

Emphasising the centuries-old people-to-people connect between India and Kenya, Shri Birla welcomed the decision of the Government of Kenya to recognize Persons of Indian Origin as an indigenous community, which further deepens relations between the two countries. He observed that both India and Kenya attach importance to democracy, inclusive development and human-centric progress. He added that this shared outlook gives the bilateral relationship special depth. Noting the influence of Mahatma Gandhi on Kenya’s struggle for freedom against colonial rule, Shri Birla observed that the Father of the Nation is regarded across the world as an enduring symbol of the peaceful struggle for truth and non-violence. He conveyed his sincere appreciation to Dr. Wetang'ula for agreeing to the installation of a statue of Mahatma Gandhi in the Parliament of Kenya.

Shri Birla highlighted that as the world’s largest democracy, guided by the Constitution since Independence, India has achieved wide-ranging development and social transformation. He added that India’s electoral process witnesses extensive participation by the people, with approximately 970 million eligible voters, of whom around 650 million cast their votes. This reflects the people’s faith and confidence in democracy.

Observing that Parliament is the highest forum of democracy, where the hopes and aspirations of citizens find a voice, Shri Birla noted that parliamentary dialogue between India and Kenya is continuously growing stronger. Referring to the constitution of Parliamentary Friendship Groups in both countries, he emphasised that regular exchanges of parliamentary delegations can add new dimensions to parliamentary relations between the two countries.

Noting that programmes for Members and officials of the Kenyan Parliament, tailored to the specific requirements of the Parliament of Kenya, have been regularly organized by the Parliamentary Research and Training Institute for Democracies (PRIDE), Shri Birla said that in the changing global environment, the use of technology has become indispensable to parliamentary functioning. He added that the Parliament of India has leveraged Artificial Intelligence in its functioning to promote transparency, efficiency, inclusivity and public participation. He informed that India would be happy to share its experiences in this area with the Parliament of Kenya.

In response, Dr. Wetang'ula thanked Shri Birla for the warm welcome. He recalled that the 28th CSPOC held in New Delhi earlier this year was one of the best organized parliamentary events. He noted that people of Indian origin have made important contributions to the growth and development of Kenya, he stated that the Indian community is active in all walks of life, including in Parliament and Government. Dr. Wetang'ula underscored the strong relationship between the two countries, especially in global multilateral forums such as the United Nations. He also called for democratic reforms of the United Nations Security Council and for India’s inclusion as a Permanent Member to better reflect the realities of the 21st century.

It was a pleasure to welcome Rt. Hon. (Dr.) Moses M. Wetang’ula, SC, EGH, MP, Speaker of the National Assembly of Kenya along with the distinguished Kenyan Parliamentary Delegation to the Parliament of India.

2299118.title: Union Minister of Textiles to inaugurate Handloom Haat: The Handloom Experience Centre at Janpath on 14 August
2299118.body_html:
Ministry of Textiles
Union Minister of Textiles to inaugurate Handloom Haat: The Handloom Experience Centre at Janpath on 14 August
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Textiles Shri Giriraj Singh will inaugurate Handloom Haat: The Handloom Experience Centre at Janpath, New Delhi, on 14 August 2026, marking a significant step towards creating a distinctive public destination for experiencing, understanding and engaging with India’s rich handloom heritage. The re-envisioned Handloom Haat will bring together heritage, knowledge, contemporary design, enterprise and retail under one roof.

The Handloom Experience Centre has been envisioned as a showcase of India’s handloom ecosystem, where traditional knowledge is not only preserved and interpreted, but actively practised, experienced and taken forward. Visitors will be able to explore the materials, processes, techniques and stories behind handwoven textiles, encounter contemporary expressions of handloom and discover products from weavers and handloom brands.

From Heritage to Contemporary Design

The inaugural showcase will feature 24 award-winning weavers through an exhibition organised by the National Handloom Development Corporation (NHDC), alongside 30+ curated brands participating through Weave The Future 5.0.

The fifth edition of ‘Weave The Future’ showcased in the ground and first floor will bring together weavers, designers, brands, researchers and other stakeholders to advance sustainable, circular and craft-led approaches to textiles. Its showcase at Handloom Haat will feature contemporary products developed through handloom and regenerative materials, with a focus on indigenous fibres, material innovation and responsible textile practices. It will also feature installations exploring India’s indigenous fibre landscape and the relationship between geography, agriculture, ecology and textile production.

The retail experience at Handloom Haat will therefore extend beyond conventional shopping, offering visitors an opportunity to discover the diversity, quality and contemporary relevance of Indian handlooms while creating greater visibility and market access for weavers and handloom enterprises.

A Multi-Layered Handloom Experience

The inauguration will offer guests a curated journey across the three floors of Handloom Haat, highlighting different dimensions of India’s handloom ecosystem.

As part of the inaugural experience, a temporary exhibition, on the ground floor, titled “Reimagining Odisha Weaves — Cloth | Craft | Creativity | Community” by Vriksh Designs will showcase how contemporary design can revitalise regional textile traditions through collaboration between designers and master weavers. The exhibition will highlight the revival of lesser-known and forgotten Odisha traditions such as Ganjam Bomkai and Dhalapathar Tapestry, alongside innovations in Ikat, Jaala and Phoda weaving, natural dyes, new colourways, textures, motifs and product forms.

The first floor will centre on the Visvakarma Gallery, a permanent gallery, bringing together rare textiles from the landmark Visvakarma exhibition series (1981–1991), which brought together weavers, designers, scholars and cultural patrons in an exploration of India’s diverse handloom traditions. Produced through Weavers’ Service Centres in close collaboration with weaving communities, these textiles demonstrate the coming together of technical skill, creative imagination and contemporary inquiry in Post-independent India. This gallery will also pay a tribute to Sant Kabir awardees and Padma Shri awardees, recognising individual practitioners whose exceptional contributions have expanded the practice, understanding and visibility of Indian handlooms.

The second floor will feature Design Conclave and an immersive experience that will take visitors on a visual and sensory journey inspired by India’s forests and the rich repertoire of animal, bird, floral and natural motifs found across diverse handloom traditions.

A New Destination for Handloom Excellence, Experience and Enterprise

The re-envisioned Handloom Haat aims to strengthen the visibility and market presence of Indian handlooms while creating opportunities for weavers, designers and handloom enterprises. By bringing together heritage, contemporary practice, retail and public engagement, it seeks to create a closer connection between India’s handloom communities and contemporary audiences.

With its integrated approach to Handloom Excellence, Experience and Enterprise, Handloom Haat at Janpath is envisioned as a prominent destination where visitors can encounter the many dimensions of India’s handloom traditions- from the people and processes behind the cloth to its contemporary possibilities.

The inauguration on 14 August 2026 will mark the beginning of this new chapter for Handloom Haat, envisioned as “The Handloom Experience Centre”, a space where India’s living textile heritage can be seen, understood, experienced and taken forward.

2299109.title: Vice President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Meets Parliamentary Delegation from Kenya
2299109.body_html:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat
Vice President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Meets Parliamentary Delegation from Kenya
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Hon’ble Vice President of India and Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today held a warm and substantive meeting with the Rt. Hon. (Dr.) Moses M. Wetang’ula, EGH, MP, Speaker of the National Assembly of Kenya, who is leading a Parliamentary Delegation from Kenya on a bilateral visit to India.

During the meeting, the Vice-President highlighted the close parliamentary ties between India and Kenya and expressed India’s readiness to share its experience in technology solutions and digital technology, including the use of digital technology leading towards a paperless Parliament. He noted the presence of an Indian-origin Member of Parliament in Kenya’s Parliamentary Friendship Group and recalled with appreciation the proposal to install a bust of Mahatma Gandhi within the premises of the National Assembly of Kenya.

The Vice-President recalled that Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had visited Kenya in 2016, followed by the visit of Hon’ble President Ruto to India in 2023.

Referring to India’s development partnership with Kenya, the Vice-President noted that several projects had been executed in the form of grant-in-aid, including the refurbishment of the Mahatma Gandhi Graduate Library of the University of Nairobi and the CT scan infrastructure at the Kenyan Navy Base, Mtongwe. He also recalled India’s assistance during the Ebola Virus Outbreak, when India delivered the first tranche of 4.5 tonnes of medical supplies.

The Vice-President highlighted India’s continued support for capacity building in Kenya. He stated that the Government of India offers around 400 scholarships, including training courses for various Government Ministries. He further noted that 20 diplomats from Kenya are undergoing capacity development in India. He informed that ICCR scholarships for long-term courses have been increased from 80 to 100 annually.

The Vice-President also highlighted the Agreement on the Digi-Locker pilot project in Kenya, which was signed during the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi. He further noted that Indian and Kenyan teams are working on the GATI Shakti project for Kenya.

The Vice-President thanked Kenya for supporting India’s candidature for the non-permanent seat in the United Nations Security Council for the term 2028–29. He sought Kenya’s support for India’s permanent membership in the United Nations Security Council.

Emphasising the historical ties between the two countries, the Vice-President noted that India and the Swahili coast had well-established trading routes for benefit of each other. He also expressed India’s hope that Kenya would join the International Solar Alliance and the International Big Cat Alliance.

The Vice President also highlighted the centuries-old people-to-people ties between India and Kenya and said that he was delighted to note that the Indian diaspora had been recognised as the 44th tribe of Kenya.

Concluding the meeting, the Vice President thanked the Kenyan Parliamentary Delegation for visiting India and conveyed his best wishes for a pleasant and productive stay. He expressed confidence that the visit would further deepen parliamentary engagement and contribute to strengthening the comprehensive partnership between India and Kenya.

2299107.title: Hon'ble Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment to chair the 5th Meeting of the National Council for Senior Citizens (NCSrC)
2299107.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Hon'ble Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment to chair the 5th Meeting of the National Council for Senior Citizens (NCSrC)
Ministry To Launch e-Book titled "SNEHA - Stories of Nurturing, Engagement, Happiness & Active Ageing"
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Hon'ble Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar will chair the 5th Meeting of the National Council for Senior Citizens (NCSrC) tomorrow at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), New Delhi.

The meeting will be attended by the representatives of Central Ministries, Departments, State Governments and Union Territories, Oldest Members of Parliament, National Commissions, experts in the field of ageing, representatives of Senior Citizens' Associations, Pensioners' Associations and Non-Governmental Organisations working for the welfare of senior citizens.

The Council will deliberate upon key issues concerning the welfare of the Senior citizens. The deliberations are expected to further strengthen inter-ministerial convergence and reinforce the Government's commitment towards ensuring a life of dignity, security, participation and well-being for senior citizens, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

On this occasion, the Ministry will also launch "SNEHA - Stories of Nurturing, Engagement, Happiness & Active Ageing", an e-book showcasing major events initiatives and achievements of the Senior Citizen Division from October 2024 to June 2026.

Pertinently, the National Council for Senior Citizens (NCSrC) reconstituted vide Gazette Notification dated 17th February, 2012, is the apex advisory body of the Government of India on issues relating to the welfare, protection and empowerment of senior citizens.

2299104.title: From Financial Barriers to Engineering Aspirations:
2299104.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Barriers to Engineering Aspirations:
How PM YASASVI Scholarship Support Helped PRINCE YADAV Pursue His B.Tech. Education
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 6:46PM by PIB Delhi


Access to quality higher education can play an important role in helping students pursue their aspirations and build better opportunities for the future. However, for students from families with limited incomes, financial difficulties can become a major challenge in meeting tuition and living expenses.

Demonstrating how scholarship assistance can help students overcome economic barriers, Prince Yadav, a 19-year-old student belonging to the Other Backward Class (OBC) category, is pursuing his B.Tech education at Maulana Azad National Institute of Technology (MANIT), Bhopal.

Coming from a family whose primary source of income is agriculture, he faced significant financial difficulties in meeting the costs of tuition and living expenses in Bhopal. Despite these challenges, Prince remained determined to become a successful engineer and contribute to technological advancements that can help make India self-reliant in technology, while also improving his family's financial situation.

In 2025-26, financial assistance of ₹1,15,400 was provided to Prince under the PM YASASVI Scholarship. The support helped meet his tuition and hostel-related expenses, significantly reducing the financial burden on his family. It also enabled him to continue his higher education without the pressure of taking an educational loan and allowed him to focus more fully on his academic pursuits.

 

With the financial burden related to his education reduced, Prince is currently pursuing his B.Tech. degree at MANIT Bhopal with greater confidence. He is maintaining a good CGPA and actively participating in technical clubs on campus. The scholarship support has helped him concentrate on his studies and continue working towards his aspirations in engineering and technology.

Expressing his contentment over the Ministry’s financial support, Prince Yadav said,

“The PM YASASVI Scholarship was a turning point in my academic journey. It completely removed the financial burden of my tuition and hostel fees, allowing me to focus entirely on my studies rather than worrying about educational loans. Currently, I am successfully pursuing my degree at MANIT Bhopal, maintaining a good CGPA, and actively participating in technical clubs on campus.” 

Prince's story highlights how timely scholarship assistance can provide meaningful support to students facing financial constraints. By reducing the pressure of educational expenses, PM YASASVI has enabled him to continue his higher education and pursue his aspiration of becoming a successful engineer, contributing to India's technological progress and supporting his family financially.

Ministry of Heavy Industries
Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) receives 20 bids under the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent (REPM)
India’s Indigenous Rare Earth Permanent Magnet Manufacturing Initiative Gains Momentum as the scheme gets overwhelming response
An important step towards strengthening the domestic REPM manufacturing ecosystem and enhancing competitiveness in the global markets
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) receives 20 bids through Global Tender on CPP portal for Selection of Manufacturers for establishing integrated Sintered NdFeB Rare Earth Permanent Magnet Manufacturing Facilities under the “Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM)”. On 26th November 2025, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi approved the “Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM)” with a financial outlay of Rs. 7,280 Crore. The Scheme Notification was issued by MHI on 15.12.2025.

Request For Proposal (RFP) was floated on CPP portal on 20th March 2026. The pre-bid conference was held on 7th April 2026. The last date for receiving bids was 12th August 2026 on CPP portal and the Technical Bids were opened on 13th August 2026 in the presence of the bidders at MHI.

The Scheme, a first-of-its-kind initiative, aims to establish a total capacity of 6,000 Metric Tons Per Annum (MTPA) of integrated Rare Earth Permanent Magnet manufacturing facilities in India, thereby enhancing self-reliance and positioning India as a key player in the global REPM market.

The scheme envisions allocating the total capacity to five beneficiaries through a global competitive bidding process. Each beneficiary will be allotted up to 1,200 MTPA of capacity.

The total duration of the scheme will be 7 years from the date of award, including a 2-year gestation period for setting up an integrated REPM manufacturing facility, and 5 years for incentive disbursement on the sale of REPM.

Rare Earth Permanent Magnets are among the most powerful magnets in the world and are widely used in electric vehicles, wind turbines, high-end electronics, aerospace and defence systems. By building a complete value chain from NdPr oxide to finished magnets in India, the Scheme is expected to significantly reduce import dependence in this sector.

This initiative by the Government of India is a landmark step towards strengthening the domestic REPM manufacturing ecosystem and enhancing competitiveness in global markets. By fostering indigenous capabilities in REPM production, the scheme will not only secure the REPM supply chain for domestic industries but also support the nation’s Net Zero 2070 commitment. It embodies the Government’s unwavering commitment to build a technologically self-reliant, globally competitive, and sustainable industrial base, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

2299072.title: IMPLEMENTATION OF SASCI SCHEME
2299072.body_html:
Ministry of Tourism
IMPLEMENTATION OF SASCI SCHEME
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 6:06PM by PIB Delhi

With the aim to develop iconic tourist centres in the country, the Ministry of Tourism issued operational guidelines along with detailed project report template under Special Assistance to the States for Capital Investment (SASCI)-Development of Iconic Tourist Centres to Global Scale initiative scheme.

As per the guidelines, the proposals were invited from the State Governments for considering financial assistance to the States under the scheme. The parameters formulated for examining the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) submitted by the States covered connectivity to the site, existing tourism eco-system at site/destination, carrying capacity, availability of utility services, project impact and value envisaged which included expected increase in tourist footfall, increase tourist spend, new employment opportunities, attracting private investment etc. Accordingly, 40 projects were sanctioned across 23 States in the country including two projects in the state of Karnataka by the Government of India under the scheme for ₹3295.76 Crore in the financial year 2024-25 with 100% central funding and the details of these projects is annexed.

Further, Department of Expenditure amended SASCI guidelines for 2025-26 and as per amended guidelines, States which did not avail funds under Part-III of SASCI 2024-25 are eligible to avail Special Assistance of not more than Rs.250 crores for tourism projects under Part-II of SASCI 2025-26. As per amended guidelines, Special Assistance of Rs.250 crores have been sanctioned and released each to Nagaland, Mizoram and Himachal Pradesh for tourism projects under Part-II of SASCI 2025-26 and the details of sanction is also annexed.

The projects sanctioned under the SASCI are regularly monitored at various levels. The Guidelines for SASCI, includes National Institutional Framework comprising of Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), Mission Directorate (MD) etc. and State Institutional Framework. The Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC) and Mission Directorate (MD) includes representatives of the Ministries/Departments concerned with Culture, Housing and Urban Affairs, Civil Aviation, Road Transport and Highways, Ports, Environment and Forests, Rural Development, Railways and the Archaeological Survey of India, among others, to facilitate convergence & coordinated development. Project DPRs are also required to incorporate the applicable statutory clearances, carrying-capacity considerations, stakeholder consultations and sustainable operation and maintenance arrangements.

The Ministry has also developed a Program Management Information System (PMIS) for monitoring of its destination development related schemes as a unified digital platform to facilitate seamless information, communication, sharing and reporting system in respect of the projects undertaken as part of its various schemes. Ministry of Tourism and SGs/UTAs including project implementing agencies are integral part of this system.

This information was given by Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a reply in Rajya Sabha today.

2299068.title: Office of Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Launches the “S&T Cluster Annual Report 2025-2026”
2299068.ministry: Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI
2299068.body_html:
Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI
Office of Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Launches the “S&T Cluster Annual Report 2025-2026”
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi

 

The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India launched the “Science and Technology (S&T) Clusters Annual Report 2025–26” under the chairmanship of Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser during a meeting held on 13 August 2026. The launch was also attended by Dr (Mrs) Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary; Dr Vishal Choudhary, Scientist-F; Dr Santhosh Nair, Scientist-D; and Dr Shefali Uttam, Technical Staff, Office of the PSA, along with the CEOs, COOs, and Principal Investigators of the eight S&T Clusters established under the Office of the PSA: Andhra Pradesh Medtech Zone (AMTZ Vizag); Bengaluru Science and Technology Cluster (BeST); Bhubaneswar City Knowledge and Innovation Cluster (BCKIC); Delhi Research Implementation and Innovation Cluster (DRIIV); Jodhpur City Knowledge and Innovation Cluster (JCKIC); Panjab University–IIT Ropar Regional Accelerator for Holistic Innovations (PI-RAHI); Pune Knowledge Cluster (PKC); and Research and Innovation Circle of Hyderabad (RICH).

During the launch, Prof. Sood emphasised stronger inter-cluster collaboration, industry engagement, and technology translation, with a focus on adapting and scaling successful regional solutions and measuring outcomes through higher TRLs, real-world validation, commercialisation, and societal and economic impact.

Dr Maini highlighted the growing maturity of the S&T Clusters through a consortium-based model and emphasised the need to prioritise the national interest while strengthening industry participation in technology validation and translation.

The Report highlights the evolving role of S&T Clusters as regional innovation ecosystems and “National Technology Accelerators”, driving technology translation through shared infrastructure, public-private partnerships, startup support, and industry engagement. Several initiatives have progressed from research and pilot validation to field deployment and commercialisation, including E-Yantram, AI-enabled Digital Podiatry Clinics, AI-enabled agriculture and weather intelligence, indigenous pacemaker components, patient-specific 3D-printed implants, ChemAmaze, and One Health initiatives, alongside national platforms such as Kalaanubhav.in and i-Passport. The Report also mentions the growing international engagement of the Clusters, including the First International Conference on S&T Clusters held in December 2025, which brought together participants from over 35 countries and resulted in 12 international MoUs, followed by collaborations with the University of Western Australia, the India-Australia Smart Farm Network and the UK Catapult Network in areas including health, emerging technologies and net-zero technologies.

The S&T Clusters also presented their international collaborations that are underway across areas such as healthcare, advanced manufacturing, smart agriculture, sustainable mobility, climate resilience, emerging technologies and capacity building. Inter-Cluster collaborations has enabled successful solutions to be replicated and scaled. The Digital Podiatry Clinic, for instance, has expanded from BeST to PI-RAHI, Kalaanubhav.in, an initiative of JCKIC, is being scaled across Clusters, and I-RISE, a program of I-STEM is strengthening access to advanced scientific infrastructure through the S&T Clusters. The i-Passport initiative of AMTZ is also being considered for national scale-up, providing innovators with access to shared infrastructure, testing, mentorship, regulatory support and industry networks.

The Report can be accessed through: https://www.psa.gov.in/CMS/web/sites/default/files/2026-08/S%26T%20Clusters%20Annual%20Report%202025-26.pdf

2299002.title: Two-day ICMR-SHINE 2026 concludes, igniting scientific curiosity across thousands of young minds
2299002.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2299002.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Two-day ICMR-SHINE 2026 concludes, igniting scientific curiosity across thousands of young minds
From remote terrains to rural regions, ICMR-SHINE takes biomedical research closer to young minds across 83 locations in 31 States and Union Territories, contributing to a Swasth and Viksit Bharat
Students gain first-hand exposure to Mobile BSL-3 laboratories in Nagpur and Gorakhpur, live scientific demonstrations and hands-on activities nationwide
Young innovators showcase public health solutions through Atal Tinkering Labs in Delhi
ICMR launched SHINE website and announced nationwide school competition on real-world public health challenges, with applications open till 11 September 2026
Schools and teachers welcome research exposure, call for more frequent engagement with students
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Health Research - Indian Council of Medical Research (DHR-ICMR) successfully concluded the second edition of ICMR-SHINE (Science & Health Innovation for the Nextgen Explorers) on 11–12 August 2026, bringing the world of biomedical and public health research closer to school students across the country. Taking forward the Prime Minister’s call to “spend a day as a scientist,” the nationwide outreach program opened the doors of ICMR laboratories to students of Classes 9 to 12, giving them an opportunity to see, experience, and interact directly with the science behind public health.

The initiative spanned 31 States and Union Territories across 83 unique locations, stretching far beyond major metropolitan centers into the quiet valleys and remote terrains of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Andamans and rural regions of Jharkand, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh. For thousands of students who had never experienced research environment, ICMR-SHINE offered a welcoming bridge into the world of biomedical inquiry. Guided by Dr Curio, the friendly official mascot featured across interactive videos, posters, and cut-outs, the atmosphere was designed to make complex science feel inviting, accessible, and fun.

In Nagpur and Gorakhpur, students stepped near state-of-the-art Mobile BSL-3 laboratories on wheels, witnessing firsthand how high-containment research travels directly to field situations. In other centers, young visitors took part in lively poster walks, live scientific demonstrations, and practical exercises on body mass index calculation and lab hygiene, learning how everyday health decisions connect to the broader picture of national public health. In Delhi, the spirit of youth innovation was on full display as students showcased creative solutions developed through Atal Tinkering Labs under NITI Aayog, proving that great scientific ideas have no age limit. 

As a part of this initiative, ICMR launched the official SHINE website (https://shine.icmr.org.in/), providing students with access to resources, program updates and opportunities related to health research. ICMR has also announced a nationwide SHINE school competition, inviting students to identify real-world public health challenges, frame research questions and propose potential solutions. The competition will take the idea of “spending a day as a scientist” a step further by encouraging students to look at the health challenges around them through the lens of scientific inquiry and innovation. Applications are open until 11 September 2026 and can be submitted on the SHINE portal.

The initiative received an encouraging response from participating schools across the country. Teachers welcomed the program for giving students valuable exposure to scientific research and laboratory work beyond the classroom, and suggested that it be held more frequently. The school competition also generated enthusiasm, with one participating school announcing that all its students would take part, with submissions counting towards their internal project assessment during school examination.

Through ICMR-SHINE, thousands of students have moved from simply learning about science to seeing it, experiencing it and asking questions about it. By taking research experiences beyond conventional centers and into schools and field locations across the country, the program is creating opportunities for young minds, regardless of where they live, to encounter science firsthand. ICMR is helping young students develop a scientific outlook, encouraging them to explore science, pursue innovation, and play a role in building a Swasth and Viksit Bharat.

2298976.title: New computer model can help trace magnetic energy builds up & forecast impact of resulting CMEs
2298976.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
New computer model can help trace magnetic energy builds up & forecast impact of resulting CMEs
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 5:02PM by PIB Delhi

A multi-institutional team of scientists have developed a three-dimensional computer simulation model that can bring scientists a step closer to forecasting the arrival and impact of Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) before they reach Earth.

CMEs are among the most dramatic and powerful events in our solar system — gigantic eruptions of magnetized plasma hurled from the Sun at millions of kilometres per hour. When directed toward Earth, they can damage satellite systems, disrupt power grids, and interfere with global communications. At the heart of these eruptions lie magnetic flux ropes (MFRs), which are twisted bundles of magnetic field lines embedded in the plasma, and are widely regarded as the primary triggers of CMEs. Yet, how the magnetic energy builds up, and is then released during CMEs has remained one of solar physics' most stubborn mysteries through the violent expulsion has been poorly understood until now.

Fig 1: Snapshots from our simulation showing a twisted magnetic structure — called a flux rope — rising through the Sun's outer atmosphere. The red threads represent the Sun's background magnetic field, while blue, green, and cyan threads trace the emerging rope from its core outward. The full animation covers about 20 hours of solar time and ends with the rope being violently ejected into space.

In order to trace the evolution of the magnetic energy to CMEs researchers at the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, an autonomous institute of the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Govt. of India, along with their collaborators, have developed sophisticated three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) computer simulation model.

This model traces, step by step, how the reconnection flux changes as a magnetic flux rope rises, stretches the surrounding ambient magnetic field, and ultimately erupts. The model begins with a realistic coronal setup of a solar atmosphere, which is threaded by a magnetic field configuration resembling a coronal streamer in observation. A twisted magnetic flux rope is gradually introduced into this from below, mimicking how new magnetic flux emerges from beneath the solar surface.

Fig 2: The reconnection engine, caught in the act. The white surface (panel a) marks the current sheet — where the Sun's magnetic field lines snap and reconnect, releasing the energy that launches a CME. The S-shaped field lines in panels (b) and (c) are the magnetic threads passing through this energy release site.

The computational work in this study was performed on the NOVA HPC facility. This high-performance computing infrastructure is hosted at the data center of the IIA.

As the flux rope rises, the team observed in their computer models that the overlying magnetic field is significantly stretched and compressed beneath it. Reconnection does not begin explosively. Instead, it starts quietly with the slow formation of a thin sheet of strong electric current, a thin layer where opposing magnetic fields are pushed together. Over time, this process intensifies, culminating in the impulsive, large-scale expulsion of the flux rope.

What makes this study published in Astrophysical Journal particularly compelling is its dual approach. The researchers not only simulated two successive flux rope eruptions in their model, but also cross-validated their findings with another researcher from the University of Helsinki, Finland, who teamed up with the Indian group to contribute analysis based on observational data from NASA's Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) and the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA), two of the most powerful instruments currently observing the Sun.

Fig 3: Seeing reconnection from Earth. Left: the flash of the flare. Right: its magnetic footprint — color-coded ribbons sweeping outward across the Sun's surface over 36 minutes. The area swept by these ribbons is our observational measure of how much magnetic flux was reconnected during the eruption.

The comparison between simulation and observation revealed a striking result: the rate of magnetic reconnection correlates the acceleration of the CME in a clear, monotonic fashion, meaning that as reconnection speeds up, so does the eruption, from start to finish. This finding establishes reconnection flux as a critical factor in determining not just whether a CME erupts, but how fast and how energetically it does so.

This work by the team comprising Dr. Samriddhi Sankar Maity (Postdoc at NASA & Georgia State University, USA), Dr. Piyali Chatterjee, IIA and Mr. Ijas S Mytheen (PhD student, Eotvos University, Hungary) and Dr. Ranadeep Sarkar from the University of Helsinki, Finland, offers important new insight into the chain of events that transforms a slowly building magnetic structure into one of the powerful explosions in our solar system.

Publication link:  https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.3847/1538-4357/ae3d9a.

*****

2298971.title: Building a Business-Ready India
2298971.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Building a Business-Ready India
Advancing Ease of Doing Business, Empowering Enterprises
Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 5:01PM by PIB Delhi

Enabling Enterprise-Led Growth

As India celebrates its 80th Independence Day, the nation continues to strengthen the foundations of a self-reliant, resilient and growing economy. The Government has undertaken reforms aimed at reducing compliance burdens, enhancing transparency, encouraging entrepreneurship and creating greater opportunities for enterprises of all sizes.

These efforts are advancing Ease of Doing Business through digital single-window systems, simplified incorporation processes, wider market access, improved access to finance and trust-based regulation.

Reforming India’s Business Environment

From digital single-window clearances to large-scale regulatory clean-ups, the focus of the reforms is on creating a predictable and facilitation-driven business environment.

  • National Single Window System (NSWS): It is a single window digital platform which guides in identifying and applying for approvals according to the business requirements. The system integrates approvals across 32 Central ministries and 34 States. It provides access to over 686 central and 7,498 state approvals. Since its launch in 2021, NSWS has granted over 8.29 lakh approvals (November, 2025).
  • Startup India (2016): The initiative aims to support entrepreneurs and build a robust startup ecosystem. It seeks to transform India into a nation of job creators rather than job seekers. DPIIT-recognised startups increased from 502 in 2016 to over 2.47 lakh as on 12 August 2026.

  • SPICe+ Form (2020): This web-based form integrates 11 services from 3 Central Government ministries and departments. The form integrates 10 essential procedures including name reservation, incorporation, DIN allotment, PAN issuance, TAN issuance, EPFO registration, ESIC registration, Profession Tax registration, Bank account opening, and GSTIN allotment, and First-Time Registration of Shops and Establishment for all new companies getting incorporated in Delhi.  It thereby, reduces procedural burden, saves time and lowers compliance costs for businesses.
  • MCA21 V3: MCA21 Project, a forward-looking, AI-driven initiative significantly enhances transparency in India’s corporate landscape. The platform is used for end-to-end registry and incorporation related services of companies & limited liability partnerships (LLPs). Between 2021 and 2025, it processed 3.84 crore filings, with 3.33 crore approved through Straight Through Process.
  • Udyam Registration (2020): It offers a free, paperless, and self-declaration-based system for MSMEs (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises).   MSME registrations on the Udyam Portal increased from 0.10 lakh in October 2020 to over 9.27 lakh by 13th August 2026.
  • Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) : Launched in 2015, BRAP promotes Ease of Doing Business by simplifying regulations and improving transparency across States and Union Territories (UTs). It covers reforms across single-window clearances, land, labour, inspections, taxation, environmental approvals and others.

Unlocking Finance for Enterprise Growth

Credit guarantees, digital lending and receivables financing are widening access to formal finance, particularly for MSMEs.

 

  • Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) : PMMY (2015) bridges the gap in financial accessibility, offering collateral-free loans up to ₹20 lakh to support non-corporate and non-farm income-generating activities. As on 27 March 2026, the scheme has sanctioned loans worth ₹40.07 lakh crore through 57.79 crore loans since inception.
  • Credit Guarantee Scheme: Enables MSEs to access credit without collateral security or third-party guarantees, with support for credit facilities of up to ₹10 crore. As of March 2026, Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) had approved cumulative coverage worth ₹13.67 lakh crore, benefiting 1.41 crore guarantees.  
  • Credit Assessment Model (CAM): Launched by Public Sector Banks in 2025, CAM uses digitally fetched and verifiable data for automated MSME loan appraisal. Between April and December 2025, over 3.96 lakh MSME applications worth ₹52,300 crore+ were sanctioned under the model.
  • TReDS (Trade Receivables Discounting System): TReDS is an electronic platform that facilitates financing and discounting of trade receivables of MSMEs through multiple financiers. Union Budget 2026–27 proposed measures to strengthen TReDS, including a credit guarantee mechanism for invoice discounting and its use for Central Public Sector Enterprise transactions. The platform has grown from strength to strength, with invoice discounting increasing from ₹40,000 crore in 2021-22 to ₹3.47 lakh crore in 2025-26.

From Compliance to Trust-Based Governance

India’s regulatory reforms are moving beyond simply digitising processes towards reducing unnecessary requirements, decriminalising minor offences and creating greater certainty for businesses.

  • Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026: Decriminalises 717 provisions and amends 784 provisions across 79 Central Acts, covering 23 Ministries. It strengthens trust-based governance by reducing criminal liability for minor and technical offences.
  • Regulatory Compliance Burden: The initiative simplifies regulations and reduces unnecessary requirements to lower compliance costs and strengthen Ease of Doing Business. More than 47,000 compliances have been reduced, including 16,108 simplified, 22,287 digitised, 4,458 decriminalised, and 4,270 redundant compliances removed as of November 2025.
  • GST 2.0: Introduced in 2017, GST replaced multiple indirect taxes with a unified national tax framework. Reforms announced in September 2025 further rationalised rates and moved towards a simplified two-rate structure, reducing compliance and transaction costs. Registered taxpayers increased from around 60 lakh in 2017 to over 1.68 crore as on 31st July 2026, reflecting deeper formalisation.
  • Faceless Assessment Scheme: The scheme eliminates physical interface between the taxpayer and tax officers. Automated case selection, random allocation and a Central Cell for taxpayer communication reduce multiple visits and waiting time. The approach promotes standardised, objective and consistent tax assessments, making tax compliance more efficient and transparent.  

Expanding Markets for Indian Businesses

India’s digital public infrastructure is opening new markets for enterprises. Investments in logistics and multimodal connectivity are helping businesses move goods faster and more efficiently.

  • Government e-Marketplace (GeM) (2016): GeM digitises public procurement and expands market access for diverse businesses. As on 6th August 2026, GeM connects more than 1.37 lakh government buyer organisations with nearly 25 lakh sellers and service providers. It facilitated cumulative procurement worth over ₹20 lakh crore+. In 2025–26, more than 75 lakh orders were executed.

 

  • PM GatiShakti (2021): It enables integrated infrastructure planning and multimodal connectivity through a unified digital platform. The platform brings together 58 Ministries/Departments and 36 States/UTs with 3,291 data layers. As of February 2026, the Network Planning Group evaluated 352 projects worth ₹16.10 lakh crore, with 201 sanctioned and out of which 167 projects are under implementation. The initiative helps businesses identify suitable locations, plan investments and access upfront multimodal connectivity and infrastructure, strengthening Ease of Doing Business.
  • Open Network for Digital Commerce (2022): It promotes open digital commerce networks and reduces dependence on individual platforms. It has 7.64 lakh+ sellers across 616+ cities, supporting wider and more inclusive market access.

Strengthening India’s Global Business Footprint

India is strengthening its position in global markets by combining export promotion with better logistics, digital trade facilitation and stronger domestic production capabilities.

  • Export Promotion Mission (2025): The mission is designed to enhance India’s export competitiveness, with a focused emphasis on MSMEs, first-time exporters, labour-intensive sectors, and exporters from interior and low-export-intensity regions. By bringing financial and non-financial support under one framework, the Mission reduces barriers to exporting and makes global market access easier for businesses.
  • Trade Connect e-Platform: Provides exporters, including MSMEs, with trade information, market opportunities and access to global buyers. It has crossed 20 lakh registered users, with 40 lakh+ Certificates of Origin issued as of August 2026.
  • ICEGATE (Indian Customs Electronic Gateway): ICEGATE enables electronic filing, duty payment, document amendments, query resolution and refund processing, making cross-border trade more efficient. Bills of Entry filings increased from over 1.43 lakhs in April 2020 to over 6.14 lakhs in June 2026, reflecting growth in digital customs processing and trade activity.

Creating an Enabling Enterprise Ecosystem

India’s Ease of Doing Business journey is evolving from simplifying individual processes to building a more responsive and enterprise-friendly ecosystem. With stronger digital infrastructure, wider access to markets and finance, and greater regulatory certainty, businesses are better positioned to seize opportunities, scale sustainably and compete globally.
