2297620.title: STRENGTHENING NARCO COORDINATION CENTRE
2297620.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
STRENGTHENING NARCO COORDINATION CENTRE
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 4:06PM by PIB Delhi

Government has strengthened inter-ministerial and inter-agency coordination through restructured 4-tier (Apex, Executive, State & District level) Narco-Coordination (NCORD) mechanism by inclusion of various stakeholders at all four levels. It provides a structured, institutionalized platform for coordination among Central Ministries, State Governments and enforcement  agencies  for  monitoring drug trafficking, precursor diversion,

demand reduction and rehabilitation, resulting in improved enforcement outcomes and intelligence-sharing. NCORD has been consistently active and functional at the Apex, Executive, State and District levels. So far, 10 Apex NCORD meetings and 7 Executive NCORD meetings have been held to guide policy formulation, enhance inter-ministerial coordination and review the overall narcotics control framework. At the operational level, 272 State NCORD meetings and 16,187 District NCORD meetings have been conducted across the country, enabling coordinated enforcement action, intelligence sharing and regular monitoring of drug trafficking trends at the grassroots level. These meetings have strengthened cooperation among agencies, facilitated joint operations and supported focused interventions against drug trafficking networks operating across States. The status of implementation of directions of NCORD Committee meetings are regularly reviewed for further necessary action. Inputs of these NCORD meetings have been proved useful in drafting the Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026–2029) by Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB). Further, an NCORD Portal has been created to act as a platform for all drug and NCB related information and also as a total Knowledge Management System (KMS) for all four tiers of the NCORD mechanism. It also acts as a repository of information on the anti-drug abuse initiatives of the Government of India. In

addition, initiatives like Madak-Padarth Nished Asoochna Kendra (MANAS) - 24x7 toll-free helpline (1933), National Integrated Database on Arrested Narco-Offenders (NIDAAN) portal, Mission SPANDAN– Partnership with spiritual institutions for awareness have emerged out of NCORD mechanism.

This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

2297619.title: INCIDENTS OF CLOUDBURSTS
2297619.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
INCIDENTS OF CLOUDBURSTS
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 4:05PM by PIB Delhi

In view of the increasing frequency and intensity of incidents of cloudbursts, flash floods, landslides and extreme rainfall in Himachal Pradesh, a Multi-Sectoral Central Team (MSCT) has been constituted. The Team comprises experts from the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), Central Building Research Institute (CBRI), Roorkee, Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune, Indian Institute  of  Technology  (IIT),  Indore,  and   other  concerned  agencies.  In addition, inputs received from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water Commission (CWC) and Geological Survey of India (GSI) have also been incorporated.

The Team has been entrusted with the responsibility of undertaking a scientific assessment of the causes of increasing extreme weather events in the State, analysing the geographical and ground conditions of the worst-affected areas, compiling and examining data received from various agencies, and recommending long-term measures to minimise the impact of such disasters.

Assessments provided by weather experts, scientific institutions and State authorities indicate that, as a consequence of climate change, the intensity and frequency of extreme rainfall events are increasing in the Himalayan region. Accelerated snowmelt and moraine instability contribute to off-season slope failures and high runoff in high-altitude zones. As per MSCT study, anthropogenic factors have also contributed to the increased risk in the region.

This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

DEVELOPMENT OF NEW WATERWAY CORRIDORS ACROSS THE COUNTRY
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 3:50PM by PIB Delhi

To promote inland water transport in the country, 111 inland waterways across India have been declared as National Waterways (NWs) vide the National Waterways Act, 2016. As on date, 32 NWs are operational for the purpose of cargo and passenger movement. Further, in pursuance of the budget announcement for 2026-27 and based on studies, 19 additional new NWs have been identified predominantly for cruise tourism and passenger ferry operations over the next five years. 2297606.title: SAGARMALA PROJECT, NATIONAL WATERWAYS AND COASTAL SHIPPING
2297606.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2297606.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
SAGARMALA PROJECT, NATIONAL WATERWAYS AND COASTAL SHIPPING
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 3:48PM by PIB Delhi

At the end of the 15th financial cycle, an independent third-party impact evaluation of the projects under the Sagarmala scheme was done by the National Productivity Council (NPC). These projects are under various pillars of Sagarmala scheme including port modernization, port connectivity, coastal community development and coastal shipping and inland waterways development. No project has been sanctioned for financial assistance under the port led industrialization pillar of Sagarmala scheme.

During financial year (FY) 2025-26, total cargo movement recorded on National Waterways (NWs) was 218 million metric tons. To promote the cargo traffic on National Waterways, a scheme (Jalvahak) for providing 35% incentive to cargo owners and introduction of scheduled service on NW-1 (Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly River System) and NW-2 (river Brahmaputra) and NW-16 (river Barak) via Indo Bangladesh Protocol by Inland & Coastal Shipping Limited (ICSL) has been approved by the Government.

The average turnaround time of Major Ports has improved to 48.84 hours in 2025-26 from 52.87 hours in FY 2021-22. The Container Port Performance Index (CPPI) published by the World Bank provides an objective and comparable assessment of container port performance based on the time vessels spend in port. As per the CPPI 2025, Jawaharlal Nehru Port ranked 22nd, comparable with Hong Kong (9th), Singapore (21st), and Shanghai (23rd).

The policy initiatives taken by the Government to attract private investment in coastal shipping and inland water transport are under:

Coastal-shipping infrastructure is strengthened under Sagarmala scheme through coastal berths, Ro-Ro/Ro-Pax and passenger jetties, port-connectivity projects.

In the Union Budget 2026-27, a Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme has been announced to incentivize modal shift of cargo from road and rail to coastal shipping and inland waterways, with the objective of increasing their combined modal share from 6 per cent to 12 per cent by 2047. The scheme is expected to expand the addressable cargo base and generate opportunities for private investment in vessels, terminals, ship repair, cargo handling and multimodal logistics.

Development of National Waterway-5 (NW-5) in Odisha to connect the mineral-rich regions of Talcher and Angul with industrial centers such as Kalinga Nagar and with the ports of Paradip and Dhamra has been announced in the Union Budget 2026-27.

A scheme for providing 35% incentive to promote the utilization of inland waterways transport sector by cargo owners and for scheduled service for cargo movement on NW-1 and NW-2 and NW-16 via Indo Bangladesh Protocol by Inland & Coastal Shipping Limited (ICSL) has been approved by the Government.

An extension of the tonnage tax scheme to inland vessels registered under the Indian Vessels Act, 2021 was announced in the Union budget 2025-26 which has benefitted the Inland vessels operating on National Waterways, rivers, and canals.

The National Waterways (Construction of Jetties / Terminals) Regulations 2025 have been notified, allowing private companies to invest in and operate Inland Waterways terminals by providing a clear regulatory framework to attract private sector investment for facilitating the growth of inland waterways sector.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha.

2297605.title: SAGARMALA STARTUP AND INNOVATION INITIATIVE
2297605.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2297605.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
SAGARMALA STARTUP AND INNOVATION INITIATIVE
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 3:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Sagarmala Startup and Innovation Initiative (S2I2) was launched on 19.03.2025 with the objective of establishing an innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem for the maritime sector in India. Maritime India Foundation (MIF), a society registered under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, 1975 and functioning under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) is the designated agency for implementing the S2I2.

Under the S2I2, Maritime Innovation Hubs (MIHs) have been established at IIT Madras, IIT Bombay, IIT Kharagpur, and the Indian Maritime University (IMU), Chennai, to support technology development, testing, validation, capacity building, and handhold startups in the development and demonstration of innovative maritime solutions. This framework enables a structured pathway from port-led problem identification to pilot execution and scale-up of startup solutions, strengthening alignment with the priorities of the maritime ecosystem.

The MIF, in collaboration with Chennai Port Authority (ChPA) and National Technology Centre for Ports, Waterways and Coasts (NTCPWC, IIT Madras), launched MAR-a-THON 2025—India's first-ever Maritime Hackathon—at IIT Madras on 25.08.2025 under the S2I2.

Following the launch of the Hackathon, the MAR-a-THON, a boot camp 2025 was organised at IIT Madras Research Park on 16th and 17th October 2025, bringing together startups, academia, industry leaders, and maritime stakeholders to address pressing maritime challenges. The response to the initiative was overwhelming, with 330 applications received from startups across India for the 51 problem statements across following six thematic areas:

Port Infrastructure
Smart & Integrated Port Operations
Integrated Logistics & Multimodal Connectivity
Green & Sustainable Maritime Sector
Advanced Safety, Security & Regulatory Compliance
Shipbuilding & Lifecycle Management

Following the evaluation by multiple Expert Committees, the event culminated in the selection of 36 startups for 40 projects, each tackling real-world operational challenges with innovative, scalable solutions poised to drive transformation across India’s maritime sector.

As part of the S2I2, Visakhapatnam Port in Andhra Pradesh has identified 04 specific problem statements.

Further, 02 startups from Andhra Pradesh have been on-boarded to develop and implement innovative solutions to the problem statements.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha.

Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 3:46PM by PIB Delhi

Lighthouses primarily serve as Marine Aids to Navigation for ensuring safe and efficient maritime navigation. In addition to this core function, the Government is actively promoting Lighthouse Tourism which is in line with its vision of preserving India's maritime heritage and promoting educational, cultural and tourism purposes under Section 23 of the Marine Aids to Navigation Act, 2021.

As part of this initiative, Lighthouse Museums have been established at Chennai, Mahabalipuram, Alappuzha, Kannur, Muttom, Dwarka and Gopnath to showcase the evolution of lighthouse technology and India's maritime heritage. Under this initiative, tourism facilities have been developed at 75 lighthouses across the country as part of the Government's vision to preserve their historical and architectural significance. Tourist facilities such as cafeterias, landscaped gardens, gazebos, children's play areas, light and sound show, internal pathways, public toilet blocks, drinking water facilities, amphitheatres and lifts have been developed at identified lighthouses. 2297570.title: Regulation and rationalisation of maximum retail prices of medicines
2297570.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals
2297570.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Regulation and rationalisation of maximum retail prices of medicines
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 3:10PM by PIB Delhi

Prices of drugs are regulated as per the provisions of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order 2013 (DPCO, 2013) which has been promulgated based on the principles of the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Policy, 2012 (NPPP, 2012). National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) under Department of Pharmaceuticals fixes ceiling prices of formulations specified in Schedule-I to DPCO and the retail price of a new drug as defined under 2(1)(u) of DPCO 2013, based on market data and as per the provisions of DPCO, 2013. The ceiling prices of scheduled drugs are applicable to all manufacturers and retail prices fixed for new drugs are applicable to applicant manufacturer and marketer and they have to sell them within the notified ceiling price or retail price (plus applicable GST) by the NPPA. However, manufacturers are free to sell at a price lower than the ceiling price for the schedule drug and retail price fixed for new drug, as per the market dynamics.

There is no restriction on manufacturer fixing different prices for same schedule formulation under different brand names as long as it is below the ceiling prices fixed by NPPA for that drug.  In case of non-scheduled formulations, a manufacturer is allowed to fix the price of the drug but are required to not increase MRP of a non-scheduled drug by more than 10% of MRP during the preceding 12 months.    Such price regulation in conjunction with various other initiative taken by government to improve the access to healthcare facilities has resulted in a decline in the share of out-of-pocket expenditure in Total Health Expenditure from 62.6% in 2014-15 to 43.4% in 2022-23.

NPPA monitors the compliance with the provisions of the DPCO, 2013 and takes appropriate action in cases of overcharging and other violations, in accordance with the provisions of DPCO, 2013, based on references received from various sources, including Price Monitoring and Resource Units set up in States, State Drugs Controllers, samples purchased from open market, reports from market database and complaints lodged through various grievance redress channels. Further, to prevent overpricing, DPCO 2013 requires every manufacturer of a formulation to print the maximum retail price on the label of the container of such formulation. No person is permitted to sell any formulation to any consumer at a price exceeding the price specified on the current price list or price indicated on the label of the container or the pack thereof, whichever is less.

In addition to regulating the prices of drugs under DPCO, 2013, various other measures have been taken by the Government to improve the access of medicines at affordable rates to the common man which, inter alia, include the following:

  1. Under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana scheme quality generic medicines is provided through more than 20,000 Janaushadhi Kendras at rates that are typically 50% to 80% cheaper than branded medicines.
  2. Under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) of the Department of Health and Family Welfare, health assurance/insurance cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year is provided for secondary or tertiary care hospitalisation, including for medicines.
  3. Under the Free Drugs Service Initiative of the National Health Mission, essential medicines list recommended under the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) are made available free of any charge at public health facilities ranging from Primary Health Centres (PHCs) to district hospitals across the country.
  4. Under the Amrit (Affordable Medicines and Reliable Implants for Treatment) initiative of the Department of Health and Family Welfare, affordable medicines are provided for the treatment of cancer, cardiovascular and other diseases, implants, surgical disposables and other consumables etc., at an average discount of up to 50% on market rates through AMRIT Pharmacy stores set up in number of hospitals and healthcare institutions.       
  5. Financial assistance is provided to poor patients belonging to families living below the poverty line, who suffer from major life-threatening diseases including cancer, under the umbrella scheme of Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi and the Health Minister’s Discretionary Grant.

This information was given by Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

2297568.title: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras
2297568.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals
2297568.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 3:07PM by PIB Delhi

Under Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), a total of 20,149 Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) have been opened across the country till 30.06.2026, out of which 1833 JAKs have been opened in the State of Kerala. The district-wise number of JAKs opened in the State of Kerala is at Annexure.

The product basket under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojna has 2,110 medicines and 315 surgicals, medical consumables and devices, covering all major therapeutic groups, such as cardiovascular, anti-cancer, anti-diabetic, anti-infectives, anti-allergic and gastro-intestinal medicines and nutraceuticals.

During the last five financial years i.e. 2021-22 to 2025-26, PMBJP has made sales of Rs. 7,873.85 crore through Jan Aushadhi Kendras across the country which has led to savings of approximately Rs. 37,200 crore to the citizens.

Government has adopted a franchise-like model for opening of Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs). Any individual entrepreneurs, non-governmental organisations, societies, trusts, firms, private companies, etc., can apply for opening of Jan Aushadhi Kendras, through the scheme’s website (www.janaushadhi.gov.in) across the country including those in Kerala. To facilitate the opening of Jan Aushadhi Kendras in the underserved areas, Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI) is regularly writing letters to the concerned administration/district magistrate for providing free space to the applicants in government hospitals.

 

To address supply gaps and ensure uninterrupted availability of products at JAKs, the following measures have been put in place:

  1. Since September 2024, stocking by JAKs of 200 commonly used medicines, consisting of the 100 top-selling medicines in the scheme product basket and 100 fast-selling medicines in the market, has been incentivised, under which JAK owners are eligible for monthly incentive based on the stocks that they maintain for these medicines.
  2. An end-to-end information-technology-enabled supply chain system connects a robust supply chain system comprising five warehouses and a growing network of distributors across the country, currently numbering 42.
  3. In addition, with a view to ensure availability of commonly used products, 400 fast-moving products are monitored regularly by Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), the scheme implementing agency, and demand for the same is estimated on a continuous basis. Further, steps have been taken to digitise the estimation method to augment the procurement process.

To ensure that only quality medicines are supplied through Jan Aushadhi Kendras, the following quality assurance mechanisms have been put in place:

(i) Procurement only from WHO-GMP certified manufacturers: Medicines are procured only from pharmaceutical units compliant with World Health Organization-Good Manufacturing Practices (WHO-GMP).

(ii) Distribution only after 100% pre-testing of all medicine batches: Random testing of 100% batches supplied at PMBI’s warehouses, and medicines are dispatched for supply to JAKs only after successful quality test.

(iii) Testing through NABL-accredited laboratories: Samples are tested only in laboratories accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), which are also assessed by PMBI for compliance with Good Laboratory Practices (GLP).

2297567.title: Shortages of essential medicines in Government hospitals and Jan Aushadhi Kendras
2297567.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals
2297567.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Shortages of essential medicines in Government hospitals and Jan Aushadhi Kendras
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 3:05PM by PIB Delhi

As per information provided by Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoH&FW), to ensure availability of essential drugs and reduce the Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE) of the patients visiting the public health facilities, Government has rolled out the Free Drugs Service Initiative (FDSI) under National Health Mission (NHM).  Under this, financial support is provided to States / Union Territories for provision of free essential medicines in public health facilities based on the requirements posed by them in their Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) within their overall resource envelope.

MoH&FW has recommended facility wise Essential Medicines List (EML) to be made available at the public healthcare facilities:

  1. Sub Health Centre Ayushman Arogya Mandir (SHC-AAMs) - 113
  2. Primary Health Centre Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (PHC-AAMs) - 179
  3. Community Health Centers (CHCs) - 301
  4. Sub-District Hospital - 318
  5. District Hospital (DHs) - 381

Support under the scheme is available for procurement of drugs and strengthening /setting up robust systems of procurement, Quality Assurance, supply chain management and warehousing, prescription audit, grievance redressal, dissemination of Standard Treatment guidelines and establishment of IT enabled platform DVDMS (Drugs & Vaccine Distribution Management System) for monitoring the real status of procurement and availability of essential medicines. To facilitate the monitoring of supply chain management activity at National level, a Central Dashboard has been developed.

Also, under National Health Mission (NHM), Common Review Missions (CRM) are conducted annually to assess and monitor the progress and implementation status of various schemes including FDSI.

Quality of drugs procured, under FDSI is ensured through the operational guidelines of the initiative that:-

  1. All drugs must be sourced from Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) compliant manufacturers through robust procurement mechanism. 
  2. Post supply testing of every batch before distributing to the health facilities.

Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), the implementing agency of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Priyojana (PMBJP), continuously monitors the availability of medicines including essential medicines at Jan Aushadhi Kendras, (JAKs) including those operating in Kerala.

The product basket under the PMBJP has 2,110 medicines and 315 surgicals, medical consumables and devices, covering all major therapeutic groups, such as cardiovascular, anti-cancer, anti-diabetic, anti-infectives, anti-allergic and gastro-intestinal medicines and nutraceuticals. Almost all generic medicines included in the National List of Essential Medicines, except lab reagents and vaccines, are part of this product basket. Continuous monitoring and appropriate corrective measures are undertaken to minimize stock shortage and ensure availability of essential medicines across the country.

In order to address any supply gaps and ensure smooth supply and availability of products at JAKs, the following measures are in place:

  1. Since September 2024, stocking by JAKs of 200 commonly used medicines, consisting of the 100 top-selling medicines in the scheme product basket and 100 fast-selling medicines in the market, has been incentivised, under which JAK owners are eligible for monthly incentive based on the stocks that they maintain for these medicines.
  2. An end-to-end information-technology-enabled supply chain system is in place to connect a robust supply chain system consisting of five warehouses and a growing network of distributors across the country, currently numbering 42.
  3.  In addition, with a view to ensure availability of commonly used products, 400 fast-moving products are monitored regularly by Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI), the scheme implementing agency, and demand for the same is estimated on a continuous basis. Further, steps have been taken to digitise the estimation method to augment the procurement process.

This information was given by Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

2297557.title: LOW PARTICIPATION IN GRAM SABHA MEETINGS
2297557.body_html:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
LOW PARTICIPATION IN GRAM SABHA MEETINGS
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 2:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has released a National Study Report on Low Participation in Gram Sabha across States and Union Territories (UTs) on 30th June, 2026, prepared by the National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (N.I.R.D.P.R).

The assessment identified multiple factors contributing to low and inconsistent participation across Gram Panchayats. These include livelihood and occupational constraints, weak awareness and inadequate communication systems, weak responsiveness to grievances, absence of line department officials, limited transparency in governance processes, inadequate follow-up actions on issues raised during meetings, etc. On women’s participation, the findings also reflected continuing barriers relating to household responsibilities, social hesitation, male dominance during discussions and limited opportunities for effective participation.

 “Panchayat”, being “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of State List of Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. Panchayats are set up and operated through the respective State Panchayati Raj Acts. States have made their own Panchayati Raj Act, subject to the provisions of the Constitution of India. As per Article 243(b) of the Constitution of India, a Gram Sabha comprises of persons (including women, youth, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and other disadvantaged sections) registered in the electoral rolls relating to the village. Article 243A of the Constitution of India states that a Gram Sabha may exercise such powers and perform such functions at the village level as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide, which ensures rural democracy, formulation of local development plans, social monitoring and accountability of Panchayats, etc.

The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has taken various steps to make the Gram Sabha a more participatory and accountable institution by circulating detailed advisories to the States/ UTs to revitalize the institution of Gram Sabhas by taking up measures such as sharing basic details of flagship schemes of the Government in Gram Sabha meetings, increasing the frequencies of Gram Sabhas, ensuring minimum quorum as provided in the State Panchayati Raj Act, preparation of regular standing agenda for the Gram Sabha, to facilitate the holding of separate Ward Sabha and Mahila Sabha meeting before Gram Sabha meetings, ensuring maximum attendance in Gram Sabha, formation and functioning of Standing Sub-Committees of Gram Sabha,etc.

The Ministry is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, namely the Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), w.e.f. financial year 2022-23, with the objective of supporting Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by imparting training to Elected Representatives (ERs) and other stakeholders to develop leadership abilities, thereby enabling Gram Panchayats to function effectively across all States/UTs. Under the scheme, capacity-building support is provided to elected representatives, functionaries, and other stakeholders of Panchayats, including women, youth, SCs, STs and other disadvantaged sections of society under different categories, viz. basic orientation and refresher programmes, thematic interventions, specialized training, and Panchayat Development Plan-related programmes, etc.

Additionally, the Ministry has launched a Specialized Training Module as a part of “Shashkta Panchayat Netri Abhiyan” for the capacity building of Women Elected Representatives of Panchayati Raj Institutions. The focus of this training module is to build the capacity of Women Elected Representatives across different aspects of rural governance and enhance their knowledge and practical skills for the effective discharge of roles and responsibilities as elected representatives, thereby promoting women-led governance.

The Ministry has also launched the Model Youth Gram Sabha (MYGS), an experiential simulation of grassroots democracy in schools, wherein schools conduct mock Gram Sabha sessions involving students in agenda setting, deliberation, budgeting and passing of resolutions, closely mirroring real Gram Sabha procedures, etc. Further, the Ministry conducts the People’s Plan Campaign (PPC), typically from 2nd October to 31st January, enabling Gram Panchayats to prepare comprehensive, inclusive and need-based development plans through active engagement of citizens, particularly via Gram Sabhas, following a structured timeline for participatory planning, situation analysis and finalization of Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs).

Further, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj has also developed digital applications under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (e-MMP) to strengthen transparency and citizen-centric governance in Panchayati Raj Institutions. The eGramSwaraj portal facilitates preparation and monitoring of GPDPs through a participatory planning process, involving the Gram Sabha. Similarly, Panchayat NIRNAY, a digital application which facilitates end-to-end digital management of Gram Sabha meetings, including scheduling, advance dissemination of agenda, recording of proceedings and decisions, etc.

This information was given by Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha on 11th August 2026.

2297553.title: E-GRAM SWARAJ AND AUDITONLINE
2297553.body_html:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
E-GRAM SWARAJ AND AUDITONLINE
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 2:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP) to strengthen digital governance in Panchayati Raj Institutions across the country. Under the project, eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline have been developed to facilitate digital planning, budgeting, accounting, audit, asset management and monitoring of Panchayat activities. Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) are prepared through a participatory planning process and uploaded on the eGramSwaraj portal.

Further, eGramSwaraj has been integrated with various Government digital platforms, including the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) for online payments and financial management, Government e-Marketplace (GeM) for procurement, BHASHINI for multilingual AI-enabled services, BSNL for BharatNet connectivity monitoring and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) for weather-related information.

The State/UT-wise details of implementation of eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline, including the State of Madhya Pradesh and the Gwalior Lok Sabha Constituency, are given at Annexure-I.

The Ministry of Panchayati Raj conducts capacity-building programmes for elected representatives, Panchayat Secretaries and other Panchayat functionaries under the Revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA). The training programmes include training on digital governance, effective utilisation of the e-Panchayat applications, preparation of Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs), data management and evidence-based planning.

The State/UT-wise details of participants trained under RGSA, including those relating to the Gwalior Lok Sabha Constituency, are given at Annexure-II. The district/ constituency-wise details are maintained by the respective State Government. The training programmes have contributed to improved adoption and utilisation of the e-Panchayat applications, enhanced digital capacity of Panchayat functionaries and strengthened transparency and efficiency in Panchayat governance.

2297526.title: Prime Minister shares an article by Union Minister on GeM transforming public procurement
2297526.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister shares an article by Union Minister on GeM transforming public procurement
Posted On: 11 AUG 2026 1:55PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today shared an insightful article by Union Minister Shri Piyush Goyal detailing the achievements of the Government e Marketplace (GeM) so far. He highlighted transparent procurement, wider participation, and better opportunities, stating that this is how GeM is transforming public procurement.

The Prime Minister noted that with technology at its core, the GeM platform has strengthened Ease of Doing Business over the last 10 years by creating a more competitive and inclusive ecosystem. He observed that it is particularly empowering MSMEs and women entrepreneurs.

In a post on X, the Prime Minister shared:

"Transparent procurement, wider participation and better opportunities... This is how @GeM_India is transforming public procurement.

With technology at its core, the GeM platform has strengthened Ease of Doing Business over the last 10 years by creating a more competitive and inclusive ecosystem, particularly empowering MSMEs and women entrepreneurs.

Read this insightful article by Union Minister Shri @PiyushGoyal to delve in detail about the achievements so far."
